docstring:
For every 64-bit key and every 64-bit input `id`, the bits of `id` above the
40-bit domain are ignored: `obfuscate(id, key) == obfuscate(id & MAX_ID, key)`,
and deobfuscating `obfuscate(id, key)` returns exactly `id & MAX_ID`; no call
panics.

pbt.assertion: prop_assert_eq!(obfuscate(id, key), obfuscate(id & MAX_ID, key)); prop_assert_eq!(deobfuscate(obfuscate(id, key), key), id & MAX_ID)

docstring:
For every 64-bit key and every 64-bit input, both `obfuscate(id, key)` and
`deobfuscate(id, key)` never panic and return a value in the 40-bit domain,
i.e. at most `MAX_ID = 2^40 - 1` (inputs above the domain are reduced, and
every Feistel round keeps both halves below `2^20`).

pbt.assertion: prop_assert!(obfuscate(id, key) <= MAX_ID); prop_assert!(deobfuscate(id, key) <= MAX_ID)

theorem_statement:
(key id : Std.U64)
    (h_id : id.val ≤ 2^40 - 1) :
    round_trip_over_the_whole_domain_spec key id
docstring:
For every 64-bit key and every id in the 40-bit domain `0..=MAX_ID`
(`MAX_ID = 2^40 - 1`), obfuscating the id and then deobfuscating the code
with the same key never panics and returns the original id: the 6-round
Feistel network `feistel_n_inv` inverts `feistel_n`.

pbt.assertion: prop_assert_eq!(deobfuscate(obfuscate(id, key), key), id)

theorem_statement:
(values : List Std.Usize)
    (h_nodup : values.Nodup)
    (h_len : values.length < 20)
    (h_range : ∀ v ∈ values, v.val < 1028)
    (h_platform : System.Platform.numBits = 64) :
    insert_contains_spec values
docstring:
Setting the bits of a set of fewer than 20 distinct keys below 1028 in a fresh
`VecBitmap::new_with_capacity(1028)` never panics, and afterwards `get(i)`
answers exactly the membership of `i` in the set, for every `i < 1028`.

pbt.assertion: for i in 0..MAX_KEY { assert_eq!(b.get(i), values.contains(&i)) } after b = new_with_capacity(MAX_KEY) and b.set(v, true) for v in &values

theorem_statement:
(elements : Slice Std.Usize)
    (h_len : elements.length < 64)
    (h_sorted : elements.val.Pairwise (fun a b => a.val < b.val))
    (i : Std.Usize)
    (h_i : i.val < elements.length) :
    binary_search_finds_index_spec elements i
docstring:
For a strictly increasing `usize` vector `elements` and any position `i`,
`binary_search_by(0, elements.len() - 1, |x| elements[x].cmp(&elements[i]))`
never panics and returns `i`, which is also the partition point of
`|x| *x < elements[i]`.

strategies.elements: arb_elements(): proptest::collection::vec(any::<usize>(), 0..64), then sort() and dedup()

pbt.assertion:
for i in 0..elements.len() { let expected = elements.partition_point(|x| *x < elements[i]); assert_eq!(expected, i);
let returned = binary_search_by(0, elements.len() - 1, |x| elements[x].cmp(&elements[i])); assert_eq!(expected, returned) }

docstring: Writing any `u128` with `LittleEndian::write_u128` into a zeroed 16-byte buffer (left-aligned: `buf[..size_of::<u128>()]`) and reading it back with `LittleEndian::read_u128` never panics and returns the same value.

strategies.n: quickcheck Arbitrary for Wi128<u128> via qc_sized(prop, 16 + 1 - 1) (the test's own `Arbitrary for Wi128<u128>` with Gen size 16 computes `max = calc_max!(u128::MAX, 16, 16) = u128::MAX - 1` and returns `(two random u64 halves) & (max - 1)`, i.e. every u128 whose bit 1 is clear)

pbt.assertion: n == LittleEndian::read_u128(&buf[..bytes]) after LittleEndian::write_u128(&mut buf[..bytes], n.clone()) with buf = [0; 16], bytes = size_of::<Wi128<u128>>()

docstring: Writing any `u64` with `BigEndian::write_u64` into a zeroed 16-byte buffer (right-aligned: `buf[16 - size_of::<u64>()..]`) and reading it back with `BigEndian::read_u64` never panics and returns the same value.

strategies.n: quickcheck Arbitrary for u64 via qc_sized(prop, ::core::u64::MAX as u64 - 1) (quickcheck 0.9 `Arbitrary for u64` with Gen size `u64::MAX - 1` samples `gen_range(0, 2^64 - 2)`, i.e. n in [0, 2^64 - 3])

pbt.assertion: n == BigEndian::read_u64(&buf[16 - bytes..]) after BigEndian::write_u64(&mut buf[16 - bytes..], n.clone()) with buf = [0; 16], bytes = size_of::<u64>()

docstring: Writing any `n < 2^72` with `LittleEndian::write_uint128(&mut buf, n, 9)` into a zeroed 16-byte buffer and reading the first 9 bytes back with `LittleEndian::read_uint128(&buf[..9], 9)` never panics and returns the same value.

strategies.n: test-local `Arbitrary for Wi128<u128>` (src/lib.rs:2358-2365) with Gen size 9 (`qc_sized(prop, 9)`): `max = calc_max!(u128::MAX, 9, 16) = (2^128 - 2) >> 56 = 2^72 - 1`, value `output & (max - 1)` for a uniform u128 `output`, i.e. every n < 2^72 with bit 0 clear

pbt.assertion: n == LittleEndian::read_uint128(&buf[..9], 9) after LittleEndian::write_uint128(&mut buf, n.clone(), 9) with buf = [0; 16]

docstring: Writing any `n < 2^24` with `BigEndian::write_uint(&mut buf, n, 3)` into a zeroed 16-byte buffer and reading the first 3 bytes back with `BigEndian::read_uint(&buf[..3], 3)` never panics and returns the same value.

strategies.n: quickcheck 0.9 `Arbitrary for u64` via `qc_sized(prop, calc_max!(super::U64_MAX, 3))`: Gen size `(2^64 - 2) >> (8 * (8 - 3)) = 2^24 - 1`, `gen_range(0, 2^24 - 1)`, i.e. n in [0, 2^24 - 2]

pbt.assertion: n == BigEndian::read_uint(&buf[..3], 3) after BigEndian::write_uint(&mut buf, n.clone(), 3) with buf = [0; 16]

theorem_statement:
(crc : Std.U32) (bytes : alloc.vec.Vec Std.U8) :
    fast_16_is_the_same_as_slow_spec crc bytes
docstring:
For every initial CRC value `crc` and every byte vector `bytes`, the
slicing-by-16 implementation `update_fast_16(crc, &bytes)` and the
byte-at-a-time implementation `update_slow(crc, &bytes)` both run without
panicking and return the same CRC-32.

pbt.assertion: super::update_fast_16(crc, &bytes) == super::update_slow(crc, &bytes)

docstring: Decoding the 32-byte little-endian encoding of the value of any `U256` `a` with `U256::from_le_slice` never panics and returns `a` itself.

strategies.a: uint(): `U256::from_le_slice(&bytes)` for `bytes in any::<[u8; 32]>()` (tests/uint.rs:60-64); ranges over every U256 value

pbt.assertion: prop_assert_eq!(a, to_uint(to_biguint(&a)))

docstring: For all `U256` values `a`, `b`, `a.wrapping_add(&b)` never panics and its value is `(a + b) mod 2^256`, the value of `to_uint(a_bi + b_bi)`.

strategies.a: uint(): `U256::from_le_slice(&bytes)` for `bytes in any::<[u8; 32]>()` (tests/uint.rs:60-64); ranges over every U256 value
strategies.b: uint(): `U256::from_le_slice(&bytes)` for `bytes in any::<[u8; 32]>()` (tests/uint.rs:60-64); ranges over every U256 value

pbt.assertion: prop_assert_eq!(to_uint(a_bi + b_bi), a.wrapping_add(&b))

docstring: For all `U256` values `a`, `b`, `a.wrapping_and(&b)` never panics and its value is the bitwise AND of the values, the value of `to_uint(a_bi & b_bi)`.

strategies.a: uint(): `U256::from_le_slice(&bytes)` for `bytes in any::<[u8; 32]>()` (tests/uint.rs:60-64); ranges over every U256 value
strategies.b: uint(): `U256::from_le_slice(&bytes)` for `bytes in any::<[u8; 32]>()` (tests/uint.rs:60-64); ranges over every U256 value

pbt.assertion: prop_assert_eq!(to_uint(a_bi & b_bi), a.wrapping_and(&b))

docstring: For all `U256` values `a`, `b`, after swapping them so that `a >= b`, `a.wrapping_sub(&b)` never panics and its value is `a - b`, the value of `to_uint(a_bi - b_bi)`.

strategies.a: uint(): `U256::from_le_slice(&bytes)` for `bytes in any::<[u8; 32]>()` (tests/uint.rs:60-64); ranges over every U256 value
strategies.b: uint(): `U256::from_le_slice(&bytes)` for `bytes in any::<[u8; 32]>()` (tests/uint.rs:60-64); ranges over every U256 value

pbt.assertion: if b > a { mem::swap(&mut a, &mut b) }; prop_assert_eq!(to_uint(a_bi - b_bi), a.wrapping_sub(&b))

docstring: For all `U256` values `a`, `b`, `a.wrapping_xor(&b)` never panics and its value is the bitwise XOR of the values, the value of `to_uint(a_bi ^ b_bi)`.

strategies.a: uint(): `U256::from_le_slice(&bytes)` for `bytes in any::<[u8; 32]>()` (tests/uint.rs:60-64); ranges over every U256 value
strategies.b: uint(): `U256::from_le_slice(&bytes)` for `bytes in any::<[u8; 32]>()` (tests/uint.rs:60-64); ranges over every U256 value

pbt.assertion: prop_assert_eq!(to_uint(a_bi ^ b_bi), a.wrapping_xor(&b))

theorem_statement:
(a b : Std.I64)
    (h_assume_b_nonzero : b.val ≠ 0)
    (h_assume_no_overflow : ¬ (a.val = -2^63 ∧ b.val = -1)) :
    i64_div_rem_euclid_matches_std_spec a b
docstring:
For `i64` operands with a nonzero divisor (excluding `i64::MIN / -1`),
dashu's `DivRemEuclid::div_rem_euclid` never panics, its result reconstructs
the dividend with wrapping `i64` arithmetic, its remainder lies in
`[0, |b|)`, and quotient and remainder agree with the Euclidean division
`div_euclid` / `rem_euclid`.

pbt.assertion: let (q, r) = a.div_rem_euclid(b); prop_assert_eq!(q.wrapping_mul(b).wrapping_add(r), a); prop_assert!((r as i128) >= 0 && (r as i128) < (b as i128).abs()); prop_assert_eq!(q as i128, (a as i128).div_euclid(b as i128)); prop_assert_eq!(r as i128, (a as i128).rem_euclid(b as i128))

theorem_statement:
(a b : Std.I64)
    (h_assume_b_nonzero : b.val ≠ 0)
    (h_assume_no_overflow : ¬ (a.val = -2^63 ∧ b.val = -1)) :
    i64_div_rem_reconstructs_spec a b
docstring:
For `i64` operands with a nonzero divisor (excluding `i64::MIN / -1`),
dashu's truncating `DivRem::div_rem` never panics, reconstructs the dividend
(`q * b + r == a`) and returns a remainder smaller than the divisor in
absolute value.

pbt.assertion: let (q, r) = a.div_rem(b); prop_assert_eq!((q as i128) * (b as i128) + (r as i128), a as i128); prop_assert!((r as i128).abs() < (b as i128).abs())

theorem_statement:
(a b : Std.U128)
    (h_assume_b_nonzero : b.val ≠ 0) :
    u128_div_rem_reconstructs_spec a b
docstring:
For `u128` operands with a nonzero divisor, dashu's `DivRem::div_rem` never
panics, and its quotient and remainder reconstruct the dividend with checked
`u128` arithmetic (`q * b + r == a`, no overflow) with `r < b`.

pbt.assertion: let (q, r) = a.div_rem(b); prop_assert_eq!((q as u128) * (b as u128) + (r as u128), a as u128); prop_assert!((r as u128) < (b as u128))

docstring:
For every `u64`, dashu's `PowerOfTwo::is_power_of_two` never panics and
returns `true` exactly when the population count `x.count_ones()` is 1.

pbt.assertion: prop_assert_eq!(PowerOfTwo::is_power_of_two(&x), x.count_ones() == 1)

theorem_statement:
(header : storage.storage_header.StorageHeader)

    (h_bad : bad_pattern.val ≠ storage.storage_header.StorageHeader.PATTERN_AT_START.val) :

docstring:
For every storage header `header` and 4-byte pattern `bad_pattern` different
from `StorageHeader::PATTERN_AT_START`, decoding `header.to_bytes()` succeeds
with `header` itself, and decoding the same buffer with its first four bytes
overwritten by `bad_pattern` fails with the
`StorageHeaderStartPatternError { actual_pattern: bad_pattern }`.

strategies.header: proptest_generators::storage_header_any() (src/proptest_generators/mod.rs:77-88): `timestamp_seconds in any::<u32>()`, `timestamp_microseconds in any::<u32>()`, `ecu_id in any::<[u8;4]>()`
strategies.bad_pattern: any::<[u8;4]>().prop_filter("pattern must not match the expected pattern", |v| *v != StorageHeader::PATTERN_AT_START)

pbt.assertion: ok case: prop_assert_eq!(Ok(header.clone()), StorageHeader::from_bytes(header.to_bytes())); error case: bytes[0..4] overwritten with bad_pattern, then prop_assert_eq!(Err(error::StorageHeaderStartPatternError{ actual_pattern: bad_pattern.clone() }), StorageHeader::from_bytes(bytes))

docstring:
Serialising an Ethernet II header to its 14 wire bytes and parsing them back
never panics and yields the original header.

strategies.input: ethernet_2_any(): source, destination in any::<[u8;6]>(), ether_type in any::<u16>() (every Ethernet2Header)

pbt.assertion: assert_eq!(input, Ethernet2Header::from_bytes(input.to_bytes()))

docstring:
Writing an Ethernet II header into a 14-byte buffer succeeds and leaves
`to_bytes()`; a shorter prefix returns `SliceWriteSpaceError` for that length.

strategies.input: ethernet_2_any(): every Ethernet2Header (source and destination any [u8; 6], ether_type any u16)

pbt.assertion: buffer of 14 zeros becomes to_bytes() after write_to_slice; for len in 0..14 the prefix write returns SliceWriteSpaceError { LEN, len, Ethernet2Header, 0 }

theorem_statement:
(input : link.linux_sll_header.LinuxSllHeader)
    (packet_type_value protocol_num : Std.U16)
    (h_packet_type_value : packet_type_value.val ≤ 7)
    (h_packet_type :
      link.linux_sll_packet_type.LinuxSllPacketType.Insts.CoreConvertTryFromU16HeaderError.try_from
        packet_type_value = ok (core.result.Result.Ok input.packet_type))
    (h_arp_hrd_type : input.arp_hrd_type.val ∈ [824, 778, 803, 770, 1])
    (h_protocol_type :
      link.linux_sll_protocol_type.LinuxSllProtocolType.Insts.CoreConvertTryFromPairArpHardwareIdU16HeaderError.try_from
        (input.arp_hrd_type, protocol_num) = ok (core.result.Result.Ok input.protocol_type)) :
    linux_sll_from_bytes_roundtrip_spec input
docstring:
Serialising a Linux cooked-capture (SLL) header with `to_bytes` and parsing the
16 bytes back with `from_bytes` never panics and returns `Ok` of the original
header, for every header built like the test generator `linux_sll_any()`.

strategies.input: linux_sll_any() (test_gens/mod.rs:161-178): packet_type = LinuxSllPacketType::try_from(v).unwrap() with v in 0..=7; arp_hrd_type in LinuxSllProtocolType::SUPPORTED_ARPHWD (NETLINK 824, IPGRE 778, IEEE80211_RADIOTAP 803, FRAD 770, ETHERNET 1); (sender_address_valid_length, sender_address) from a 0..8 byte vec zero-padded to 8; protocol_type = LinuxSllProtocolType::try_from((arp_hrd_type, protocol_num)).unwrap() with protocol_num in any::<u16>()

pbt.assertion: assert_eq!(input, LinuxSllHeader::from_bytes(input.to_bytes()).unwrap())

theorem_statement:
(header : net.ipv4_header.Ipv4Header)
    (h_dscp : header.dscp.val ≤ 63)
    (h_frag : header.fragment_offset.val < 2^13)
    (h_options_len : header.options.len.val ≤ 36 ∧ header.options.len.val % 4 = 0)
    (h_total_lo : 20 + header.options.len.val ≤ header.total_len.val)
    (h_total_hi : header.total_len.val < 2^16 - 1) :
    ipv4_payload_len_spec header
docstring:
`Ipv4Header::payload_len` equals `total_len - 20 - options.len() as u16` when
the total length covers the header, and returns `LenError` for every smaller
`total_len`.

strategies.header: ipv4_any(): dscp in 0..=63, ecn in 0..=3, fragment_offset bits [0,13), options length in {0,4,...,36}, total_len in (20 + options.len())..u16::MAX, other fields full range

pbt.assertion: payload_len().unwrap() == total_len - 20 - (options.len() as u16); for bad_len in 0..(header_len() as u16), payload_len() on total_len = bad_len is LenError { header_len(), bad_len, Ipv4HeaderTotalLen, Ipv4Packet, 0 }

docstring:
`Ipv6RawExtHeader::new_raw` round-trips `payload()`, rejects prefixes shorter
than 6 bytes, rejects a 2047-byte payload, and rejects the unaligned lengths
the test builds by extending the serialized header.

strategies.header: ipv6_raw_ext_any(): next_header any u8, header_length any u8, payload a vec of length header_length * 8 + 6 passed to new_raw

pbt.assertion: new_raw(next, payload()) is Ok with the same next_header and payload(); prefixes of length 0..6 are TooSmall; a 2047-byte slice is TooBig; for offset in 1..8, when offset + header_len < MAX_LEN, the popped-and-pushed buffer is Unaligned

theorem_statement:
(header : net.ipv6_header.Ipv6Header) (dscp : net.ip_dscp.IpDscp)
    (h_dscp : dscp.val ≤ 63) (h_flow : header.flow_label.val ≤ 2^20 - 1) :
    ipv6_set_dscp_spec header dscp
docstring:
Before `set_dscp`, `dscp()` agrees with `IpDscp::try_new(traffic_class >> 2)`;
afterwards both equal the value that was written.

strategies.header: ipv6_any(): traffic_class any u8, flow_label in 0..=0xFFFFF, payload_length and hop_limit any, addresses any [u8; 16]

pbt.assertion: dscp() == try_new(traffic_class >> 2).unwrap() before set_dscp; afterwards try_new(traffic_class >> 2).unwrap() == dscp and dscp() == dscp

docstring:
`set_flags` stores the low 4 bits of `value` in the high nibble of
`raw_byte_8` and leaves the low nibble unchanged.

pbt.assertion: after set_flags(value), flags() == value & 0b0000_1111 and the bits outside RAW_BYTE_8_MASK_FLAGS are unchanged

docstring:
Dividing by the precomputed `DividerU64::divide_by(11)` (the 64-bit-magic
`Fast` path) never panics and agrees with `n / 11`.

pbt.assertion: assert_eq!(DividerU64::divide_by(11).divide(n), n / 11)

docstring:
Dividing by the precomputed `DividerU64::divide_by(7)` (the 65-bit-magic
`General` path) never panics and agrees with `n / 7`.

pbt.assertion: assert_eq!(DividerU64::divide_by(7).divide(n), n / 7)

theorem_statement:
(n d : Std.U64)
    (h_n : n.val < 2^64 - 1)
    (h_d_lo : 1 ≤ d.val) (h_d_hi : d.val < 2^64 - 1) :

docstring:
For every divisor `d` and dividend `n` drawn from the property-test
strategies, precomputing `DividerU64::divide_by(d)` and dividing `n` with it
never panics and returns exactly `n / d`.

pbt.assertion: assert_eq!(DividerU64::divide_by(d).divide(n), n / d)

theorem_statement:
(a b : Std.U64)
    (h_assume_a : a.val < 2^64 - 2^32 + 1)
    (h_assume_b : b.val < 2^64 - 2^32 + 1) :
    add_matches_naive_spec a b
docstring: The branch-free Goldilocks addition `algo::add` equals `(a + b) mod MODULUS` on reduced inputs.

pbt.assertion: assert_eq!(add(a, b), (u128::from(a) + u128::from(b)).rem_euclid(u128::from(MODULUS)) as u64)

docstring:
`Field::new(n)` (u128 `n * MONT_R1 % MODULUS`) and `Field::from(n)` (`mont_mul(reduce_64(n), MONT_R2)`)
produce the same Montgomery representative, and `u64::from` of it gives back `n`.

pbt.assertion: let a = Field::new(n); let b = Field::from(n); assert_eq!(a, b); assert_eq!(u64::from(a), n)

theorem_statement:
(a b c : Std.U64)

strategies.a: any::<Field>() via the test's Arbitrary impl: (0..algo::MODULUS).prop_map(Field)
strategies.b: any::<Field>() via the test's Arbitrary impl: (0..algo::MODULUS).prop_map(Field)

pbt.assertion: let ab = a * b; let ba = b * a; assert_eq!(ab, ba)

theorem_statement:
(a b : Std.U64)

pbt.assertion: assert_eq!(sub(a, b), (i128::from(a) - i128::from(b)).rem_euclid(i128::from(MODULUS)) as u64)

theorem_statement:
(x d : Std.Usize)
    (h_d_lo : 1 ≤ d.val) (h_d_hi : d.val < 999999) :
    ceil_div_matches_slow_spec x d
docstring:
For every `usize` dividend `x` (any platform width) and divisor `d` in
`1..999999`, the wrapping fast path `ceil_div(x, d)` never panics and returns
the same value as the reference `ceil_div_slow(x, d) = x / d + (x % d > 0)`.

pbt.assertion: prop_assert_eq!(ceil_div_slow(x, d), ceil_div(x, d))

theorem_statement:
(x d : Std.U64)
    (h_d_lo : 1 ≤ d.val) (h_d_hi : d.val < 999999) :
    ceil_div_u64_matches_slow_spec x d
docstring:
For every `u64` dividend `x` and divisor `d` in `1..999999`, the wrapping
fast path `ceil_div_u64(x, d)` never panics and returns the same value as the
reference `ceil_div_u64_slow(x, d) = x / d + (x % d > 0)`.

pbt.assertion: prop_assert_eq!(ceil_div_u64_slow(x, d), ceil_div_u64(x, d))

let total_count = x.count_ones() as usize; for i in 0..total_count { let r = x.select_ones(i as u32).unwrap() as usize; assert_eq!(Some(i as u32), x.rank_ones(r)); assert_eq!(Some(true), x.get(r)); } assert_eq!(None, x.select_ones(total_count as u32));

docstring:
For every word `x` and all bit indices `i, j < 64`, `Word::set(i, true)` and
`Word::set(i, false)` succeed (return `Some(())`), after which `get(i)` reports
the written bit and `get(j)` for `j ≠ i` reports the original bit of `x`.

pbt.assertion: (0..x.len()).all(|i| ... (0..x.len()).all(|j| if i == j { set_true.get(j).unwrap() == true && set_false.get(j).unwrap() == false } else { set_true.get(j) == x.get(j) && set_false.get(j) == x.get(j) }))

theorem_statement:
(t : civil.time.Time)
    (h_hour : 0 ≤ t.hour.val ∧ t.hour.val ≤ 23)
    (h_minute : 0 ≤ t.minute.val ∧ t.minute.val ≤ 59)
    (h_second : 0 ≤ t.second.val ∧ t.second.val ≤ 59)

panics, and applying it with `apply_u128` to `(a, b)` yields `(c, d)` with
`c >= d`, `c = gcd(a, b)` and `d = 0`.

docstring:
For any two sorted, deduplicated `i32` slices `a` and `b`, iterating
`Union { a, b }` (`into_iter`, then `next` until `None`, i.e. `collect`) never
panics and yields exactly the elements of the `BTreeSet` union of `a` and `b`,
in increasing order.

pbt.assertion: Union { a: &a, b: &b }.into_iter().cloned().collect::<Vec<i32>>().as_slice() == BTreeSet::from_iter(a).union(&BTreeSet::from_iter(b)).cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>().as_slice()

docstring:
For every 64-bit word, Vigna's broadword population count `count_ones`
(SWAR: 2-bit, 4-bit and byte partial sums, then a wrapping multiplication by
`L8 = 0x0101_0101_0101_0101` and a shift by 56) never panics and returns the
same number as the standard `u64::count_ones`.

pbt.assertion: count_ones(word) == word.count_ones() as usize

docstring:
The broadword "parallel unsigned ≤" on the eight bytes of two words,
`u_le8(x, y) = ((((y | H8) - (x & !H8)) | (x ^ y)) ^ (x & !y)) & H8`, never
panics and sets byte `i` of the result to `0x80` exactly when byte `i` of `x`
is at most byte `i` of `y`.

pbt.assertion: for i in 0..8 { (n.get_bits(8 * i, 8) <= m.get_bits(8 * i, 8)) == (u_le8(n, m).get_bits(8 * i, 8) == 0x80) }

docstring:
The broadword "parallel > 0" `u_nz8(n) = (((n | H8) - L8) | n) & H8` never
panics and, for each of the eight bytes, sets byte `i` of the result to
`0x80` exactly when byte `i` of `n` is non-zero.

strategies.(n0, n1, n2, n3): arbitrary (u64, u64, u64, u64), hashed with DefaultHasher into the tested word n

pbt.assertion: for i in 0..8 { (n.get_bits(8 * i, 8) != 0) == (u_nz8(n).get_bits(8 * i, 8) == 0x80) }

docstring:
For every `i64` value `x`, the branch-free `Fits64` encoding into a `u64`
(`x ↦ 2x` for `x ≥ 0`, `x ↦ 2·!x + 1` for `x < 0`, selected with bit masks)
never panics, `from_u64` decodes it back to `x`, and re-encoding the decoded
value reproduces the same word.

pbt.assertion: test_fits64(x), i.e. assert_eq!(x, i64::from_u64(x.to_u64())); assert_eq!(x.to_u64(), i64::from_u64(x.to_u64()).to_u64())
